### DPI Inspector & Setter
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/image/dpi/
- Category: Resize & Prepare
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Read the embedded DPI/PPI of PNG and JPEG files, inspect pixel dimensions, and write a corrected DPI copy.
- What it does: 
- Inputs: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF, SVG, AVIF
- Outputs: report, image
- How to use:
  1. Upload a PNG or JPEG. The tool reads the PNG pHYs chunk or the JPEG JFIF/EXIF density fields.
  2. Compare the embedded DPI with the pixel dimensions and the physical print size the tool reports.
  3. If you need a corrected copy, enable writing and enter the target DPI.
  4. Download the rewritten file. A verification pass re-reads the output and shows the written value.
- Common uses: Check whether a printer-ready file really says 300 DPI.; Correct a 72 DPI screenshot for a print layout.; Confirm physical dimensions before ordering a print.
- Limits: Changing DPI metadata does not add pixels or improve print quality; it only changes the stated physical size. Some cameras and editors omit density metadata entirely. The setter supports PNG and JPEG only. CMYK and embedded ICC profiles are reported but not colour-managed.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding all run inside your browser using Canvas and File APIs. The file is never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench, and the result exists only in a temporary object URL until you download it or close the page.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Does DPI Inspector & Setter upload my images?
    A: Decoding, editing and encoding all run inside your browser using Canvas and File APIs. The file is never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench, and the result exists only in a temporary object URL until you download it or close the page.
  - Q: What limits apply to DPI Inspector & Setter?
    A: Changing DPI metadata does not add pixels or improve print quality; it only changes the stated physical size. Some cameras and editors omit density metadata entirely. The setter supports PNG and JPEG only. CMYK and embedded ICC profiles are reported but not colour-managed.
  - Q: Is DPI Inspector & Setter free to use?
    A: Yes. The tool runs locally in your browser with no account, subscription or watermark on your output. Bench is supported by the rest of its free utility catalogue.

### Image Converter
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/image/convert/
- Category: Convert
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Convert between JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, BMP, TIFF, GIF and ICO, and rasterise SVG, with batch output and transparent handling.
- What it does: 
- Inputs: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF, SVG, AVIF
- Outputs: image, zip
- How to use:
  1. Drop one or more images. Bench sniffs the real format from the file bytes and decodes it before conversion.
  2. Pick the destination format. JPEG flattens transparency onto the chosen background; PNG, WebP and AVIF keep it.
  3. For SVG input, set a raster width or leave 0 to use the document's intrinsic size.
  4. Run the conversion and download one file or all successful outputs as a ZIP.
- Common uses: Convert PNG screenshots to compact WebP.; Rasterise a logo SVG for a site that needs PNG.; Turn a batch of photos into JPEG for a print shop.
- Limits: Animated GIF stays a single frame, and animation is not preserved when converting to other formats. HEIC/HEIF input is not decoded because no decoder is bundled; those files are rejected with an explanation. TIFF output is uncompressed and therefore large. AVIF output is only produced when the browser exposes an AVIF encoder.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding all run inside your browser using Canvas and File APIs. The file is never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench, and the result exists only in a temporary object URL until you download it or close the page.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Does Image Converter upload my images?
    A: Decoding, editing and encoding all run inside your browser using Canvas and File APIs. The file is never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench, and the result exists only in a temporary object URL until you download it or close the page.
  - Q: What limits apply to Image Converter?
    A: Animated GIF stays a single frame, and animation is not preserved when converting to other formats. HEIC/HEIF input is not decoded because no decoder is bundled; those files are rejected with an explanation. TIFF output is uncompressed and therefore large. AVIF output is only produced when the browser exposes an AVIF encoder.
  - Q: Is Image Converter free to use?
    A: Yes. The tool runs locally in your browser with no account, subscription or watermark on your output. Bench is supported by the rest of its free utility catalogue.

### Image to PDF
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/image/image-to-pdf/
- Category: Convert
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Combine JPEG, PNG, WebP or rasterised SVG images into a single PDF, one page per image or fitted to A4/Letter.
- What it does: 
- Inputs: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF, SVG, AVIF
- Outputs: document
- How to use:
  1. Add images in the order you want them to appear. The file list is processed in that order.
  2. Choose image-sized pages for exact aspect ratios, or A4/Letter for a document with optional margins.
  3. Set the internal JPEG quality. Higher quality makes a larger PDF.
  4. Run the export and download the finished PDF. Pages are assembled locally from real JPEG image streams.
- Common uses: Turn a set of photos into one document.; Package scanned pages for email.; Create a simple portfolio PDF without an upload service.
- Limits: The PDF contains raster images, not searchable text or vector objects. Transparency is flattened onto white. Orientation is taken from the decoded image, so EXIF-rotated phone photos are normalised. A maximum of 40 pages is enforced to keep memory use bounded.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding all run inside your browser using Canvas and File APIs. The file is never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench, and the result exists only in a temporary object URL until you download it or close the page.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Does Image to PDF upload my images?
    A: Decoding, editing and encoding all run inside your browser using Canvas and File APIs. The file is never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench, and the result exists only in a temporary object URL until you download it or close the page.
  - Q: What limits apply to Image to PDF?
    A: The PDF contains raster images, not searchable text or vector objects. Transparency is flattened onto white. Orientation is taken from the decoded image, so EXIF-rotated phone photos are normalised. A maximum of 40 pages is enforced to keep memory use bounded.
  - Q: Is Image to PDF free to use?
    A: Yes. The tool runs locally in your browser with no account, subscription or watermark on your output. Bench is supported by the rest of its free utility catalogue.

### Base64 & Data URI Converter
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/image/base64/
- Category: Convert
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Encode an image to Base64 or a data URI, or decode Base64 back into a real, decodable image file.
- What it does: 
- Inputs: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, SVG
- Outputs: text, image
- How to use:
  1. Choose encode to turn an uploaded image into Base64 text and a ready-to-paste data URI.
  2. Choose decode and paste a raw Base64 string or a complete data URI.
  3. For raw Base64 without a MIME prefix, select the expected output type.
  4. Copy the text or download the decoded image. The tool verifies that decoded bytes actually match the chosen image type.
- Common uses: Embed a tiny icon in CSS.; Recover an image from an API response.; Generate a data URI for an email template.
- Limits: Base64 inflates data by roughly 33 percent, so it is unsuitable for large images. Data URIs increase HTML/CSS size and block parsing; use them only for small assets. Decoding rejects malformed input and does not guess arbitrary binary formats.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding all run inside your browser using Canvas and File APIs. The file is never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench, and the result exists only in a temporary object URL until you download it or close the page.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Does Base64 & Data URI Converter upload my images?
    A: Decoding, editing and encoding all run inside your browser using Canvas and File APIs. The file is never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench, and the result exists only in a temporary object URL until you download it or close the page.
  - Q: What limits apply to Base64 & Data URI Converter?
    A: Base64 inflates data by roughly 33 percent, so it is unsuitable for large images. Data URIs increase HTML/CSS size and block parsing; use them only for small assets. Decoding rejects malformed input and does not guess arbitrary binary formats.
  - Q: Is Base64 & Data URI Converter free to use?
    A: Yes. The tool runs locally in your browser with no account, subscription or watermark on your output. Bench is supported by the rest of its free utility catalogue.

- Status: Ready
- Summary: Split an image into a rows x columns grid of equal tiles and download every tile in a ZIP.

  2. Choose the number of rows and columns. A 3 x 3 grid produces nine tiles.
  3. Select the tile format and run the splitter.
  4. Download the ZIP. Each tile is named with its row and column position.
- Common uses: Create an Instagram grid from one photo.; Cut a poster into printable panels.; Build a puzzle-like tile set.
- Limits: Tiles are equal-sized slices and may not divide exactly at the edges; remainder pixels stay with the final row/column. There is no overlap or seam blending. A maximum of 20 x 20 tiles per image is enforced.

  - Q: Does Image Splitter & Grid Cutter upload my images?

  - Q: What limits apply to Image Splitter & Grid Cutter?
    A: Tiles are equal-sized slices and may not divide exactly at the edges; remainder pixels stay with the final row/column. There is no overlap or seam blending. A maximum of 20 x 20 tiles per image is enforced.

    A: Yes. The tool runs locally in your browser with no account, subscription or watermark on your output. Bench is supported by the rest of its free utility catalogue.

- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/image/metadata-viewer/
- Category: Metadata & Privacy
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Inspect EXIF, GPS, camera details, dimensions, transparency, colour profile presence and embedded DPI in JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP and TIFF files.
- What it does: 
- Inputs: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF, SVG, AVIF
- Outputs: report
- How to use:
  1. Upload one or more images.
  2. Read the decoded dimensions, real detected format, transparency status and byte size.
  3. For JPEG/TIFF, inspect camera make/model, capture date, orientation, resolution and GPS coordinates when present.
  4. Download the report as JSON or text. The report never includes image bytes.
- Common uses: Check whether a photo contains location data.; Read camera settings from a JPEG.; Inspect why a print file reports the wrong DPI.
- Limits: The parser reads common EXIF and PNG/WebP header fields, not every proprietary maker note. Colour profiles are detected by presence, not interpreted, so CMYK conversions are not offered. GPS values are shown as stored; the tool does not map them or verify accuracy.

  - Q: What limits apply to Metadata & EXIF Viewer?
    A: The parser reads common EXIF and PNG/WebP header fields, not every proprietary maker note. Colour profiles are detected by presence, not interpreted, so CMYK conversions are not offered. GPS values are shown as stored; the tool does not map them or verify accuracy.

- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/image/strip-metadata/
- Category: Metadata & Privacy
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Remove EXIF, GPS, camera and embedded metadata by re-encoding the image, then verify the exported file no longer carries a JPEG EXIF block.
- What it does: 
- Inputs: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF, SVG, AVIF
- Outputs: image, zip
- How to use:
  1. Upload photos or screenshots and choose the output format.
  2. Run the remover. Re-encoding drops EXIF, GPS, XMP and most ancillary chunks.
  3. Read the verification line: Bench re-scans the encoded bytes for an EXIF signature.
  4. Download the cleaned file and, for sensitive material, check it again with the Metadata Viewer.
- Common uses: Share a photo without home GPS coordinates.; Clean images before publishing a listing.; Remove camera details from a screenshot.
- Limits: Re-encoding removes metadata that Canvas does not copy, which covers EXIF/GPS in practice but is not a formal guarantee for every proprietary chunk in every format. Transparency requires PNG/WebP. Removing metadata does not remove visible identifying details such as faces, reflections or document text.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding all run inside your browser using Canvas and File APIs. The file is never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench, and the result exists only in a temporary object URL until you download it or close the page.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Does EXIF & GPS Remover upload my images?
    A: Decoding, editing and encoding all run inside your browser using Canvas and File APIs. The file is never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench, and the result exists only in a temporary object URL until you download it or close the page.
  - Q: What limits apply to EXIF & GPS Remover?
    A: Re-encoding removes metadata that Canvas does not copy, which covers EXIF/GPS in practice but is not a formal guarantee for every proprietary chunk in every format. Transparency requires PNG/WebP. Removing metadata does not remove visible identifying details such as faces, reflections or document text.
  - Q: Is EXIF & GPS Remover free to use?

### Image Hash Generator
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/image/image-hash/
- Category: Metadata & Privacy
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Generate exact SHA-256 hashes plus perceptual average and difference hashes for image identity and similarity checks.
- What it does: 
- Inputs: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF, SVG, AVIF
- Outputs: report
- How to use:
  1. Upload one or more images.
  2. Bench hashes the original file bytes for SHA-256 and samples a 9 x 8 grayscale grid for dHash.
  3. Download the JSON or CSV report.
  4. Use SHA-256 for exact identity and the perceptual hashes for near-duplicate grouping.
- Common uses: Record a stable fingerprint before editing.; Find near-duplicate exports.; Compare two files without uploading them.
- Limits: SHA-256 changes completely after any re-encode. Perceptual hashes are similarity heuristics and can produce false matches on flat or highly repetitive images. They are not cryptographic proofs and should not be used for forensic attribution.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding all run inside your browser using Canvas and File APIs. The file is never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench, and the result exists only in a temporary object URL until you download it or close the page.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Does Image Hash Generator upload my images?
    A: Decoding, editing and encoding all run inside your browser using Canvas and File APIs. The file is never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench, and the result exists only in a temporary object URL until you download it or close the page.
  - Q: What limits apply to Image Hash Generator?
    A: SHA-256 changes completely after any re-encode. Perceptual hashes are similarity heuristics and can produce false matches on flat or highly repetitive images. They are not cryptographic proofs and should not be used for forensic attribution.
  - Q: Is Image Hash Generator free to use?
    A: Yes. The tool runs locally in your browser with no account, subscription or watermark on your output. Bench is supported by the rest of its free utility catalogue.

### Duplicate & Similar Photo Finder
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/image/duplicate-finder/
- Category: Metadata & Privacy
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Find byte-identical duplicates and visually similar photos using SHA-256 and perceptual hashing, entirely in the browser.
- What it does: 
- Inputs: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF, SVG, AVIF
- Outputs: report, zip
- How to use:
  1. Add a folder or a batch of photos.
  2. Bench computes SHA-256 for exact matches and a 64-bit perceptual hash for near matches.
  3. Review the groups. The first file in a group is the suggested original; later files are duplicates or variants.
  4. Download the report, and optionally a ZIP containing the files Bench marked as unique.
- Common uses: Clean up repeated downloads.; Find resized copies of the same photo.; Review a client folder for accidental duplicates.
- Limits: Similarity detection compares downscaled grayscale fingerprints, so rotations, crops and severe colour edits can reduce the score. It does not read EXIF dates or delete files automatically. Check each group before discarding anything, especially when similar-looking graphics are intentionally repeated.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding all run inside your browser using Canvas and File APIs. The file is never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench, and the result exists only in a temporary object URL until you download it or close the page.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Does Duplicate & Similar Photo Finder upload my images?
    A: Decoding, editing and encoding all run inside your browser using Canvas and File APIs. The file is never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench, and the result exists only in a temporary object URL until you download it or close the page.
  - Q: What limits apply to Duplicate & Similar Photo Finder?
    A: Similarity detection compares downscaled grayscale fingerprints, so rotations, crops and severe colour edits can reduce the score. It does not read EXIF dates or delete files automatically. Check each group before discarding anything, especially when similar-looking graphics are intentionally repeated.
  - Q: Is Duplicate & Similar Photo Finder free to use?
    A: Yes. The tool runs locally in your browser with no account, subscription or watermark on your output. Bench is supported by the rest of its free utility catalogue.

### SVG Optimiser & Validator
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/image/svg-optimizer/
- Category: Create & Developer
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Remove scripts, event handlers and dangerous URLs, validate basic SVG structure, and minify markup for safer embedding.
- What it does: 
- Inputs: SVG
- Outputs: text
- How to use:
  1. Upload SVG files or paste is not required; the tool uses file input.
  2. Bench rejects scripts, foreignObject, inline event handlers and javascript:/data URLs in links.
  3. Choose minification and comment removal.
  4. Download the cleaned SVG. The report shows removed elements and the before/after size.
- Common uses: Remove unsafe markup before publishing an SVG.; Reduce a hand-authored SVG's size.; Check why an SVG fails to render.
- Limits: Sanitising is defensive cleanup, not a formal security audit. Complex SVG features such as external references, embedded fonts and animation are not optimised and may be removed or preserved conservatively. This is an optimiser and sanitiser, not a vector tracer, and it never turns a raster image into true vectors.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding all run inside your browser using Canvas and File APIs. The file is never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench, and the result exists only in a temporary object URL until you download it or close the page.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Does SVG Optimiser & Validator upload my images?

Complex SVG features such as external references, embedded fonts and animation are not optimised and may be removed or preserved conservatively. This is an optimiser and sanitiser, not a vector tracer, and it never turns a raster image into true vectors.
  - Q: Is SVG Optimiser & Validator free to use?

### Image Inspector & Diagnostics
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/image/inspection/
- Category: Diagnostics
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Check real file signatures, decodability, dimensions, transparency, orientation and compression advice, and get a plain-English failure diagnosis.
- What it does: 
- Inputs: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF, SVG, AVIF
- Outputs: report
- How to use:
  1. Upload the file that is causing trouble.
  2. Bench sniffs the signature independently of the extension and attempts a real decode.
  3. Read dimensions, transparency, orientation, profile presence and a compression recommendation.
  4. If decoding fails, the report explains whether the container is malformed, unsupported or simply not an image.
- Common uses: Diagnose a file that a website rejects.; Check whether a PNG really has transparency.; Decide whether re-encoding will help.
- Limits: This is inspection and heuristic advice, not forensic verification or guaranteed repair. It does not parse every vendor-specific chunk, and a successful decode does not prove that a file is free of hidden corruption. Compression advice is based on format and pixel count, not a visual quality judgment.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding all run inside your browser using Canvas and File APIs. The file is never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench, and the result exists only in a temporary object URL until you download it or close the page.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Does Image Inspector & Diagnostics upload my images?
    A: Decoding, editing and encoding all run inside your browser using Canvas and File APIs. The file is never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench, and the result exists only in a temporary object URL until you download it or close the page.
  - Q: What limits apply to Image Inspector & Diagnostics?
    A: This is inspection and heuristic advice, not forensic verification or guaranteed repair. It does not parse every vendor-specific chunk, and a successful decode does not prove that a file is free of hidden corruption. Compression advice is based on format and pixel count, not a visual quality judgment.
  - Q: Is Image Inspector & Diagnostics free to use?
    A: Yes. The tool runs locally in your browser with no account, subscription or watermark on your output. Bench is supported by the rest of its free utility catalogue.

### Corruption Recovery (Best Effort)
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/image/recovery/
- Category: Diagnostics
- Status: Experimental
- Summary: Attempt a best-effort decode and re-encode of a damaged image, with an honest report when recovery is impossible.
- What it does: 
- Inputs: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF, SVG, AVIF
- Outputs: image, report
- How to use:
  1. Upload the damaged image.
  2. Bench checks the file signature and asks the browser decoder to decode it.
  3. If a partial or complete image can be decoded, it is re-encoded without the damaged container structure.
  4. If decoding fails, no output is invented; the report explains the failure and suggests alternate recovery paths.
- Common uses: Salvage an image that partially opens.; Normalise a file with a damaged header.; Get a clear explanation when recovery is impossible.
- Limits: Experimental and strictly best effort. This tool cannot reconstruct missing pixel data, repair truncated entropy streams or guarantee recovery. It re-encodes whatever the browser can decode, so some corruption is simply discarded. Keep the original file and never rely on a repaired copy as the only version.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding all run inside your browser using Canvas and File APIs. The file is never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench, and the result exists only in a temporary object URL until you download it or close the page.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Does Corruption Recovery (Best Effort) upload my images?
    A: Decoding, editing and encoding all run inside your browser using Canvas and File APIs. The file is never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench, and the result exists only in a temporary object URL until you download it or close the page.
  - Q: What limits apply to Corruption Recovery (Best Effort)?
    A: Experimental and strictly best effort. This tool cannot reconstruct missing pixel data, repair truncated entropy streams or guarantee recovery. It re-encodes whatever the browser can decode, so some corruption is simply discarded. Keep the original file and never rely on a repaired copy as the only version.
  - Q: Is Corruption Recovery (Best Effort) free to use?
    A: Yes. The tool runs locally in your browser with no account, subscription or watermark on your output. Bench is supported by the rest of its free utility catalogue.

## Bench Audio Toolkit

Hub: https://bench.progeni.live/audio/
Public tools: 48 (43 implemented, 5 experimental).

### Audio Converter
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/audio/convert/
- Category: Convert
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Convert between MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG, Opus and AIFF with a real encoder and an exact output size.
- What it does: Decodes your file and re-encodes it in the format you choose using the FFmpeg.wasm engine that runs on your device. Lossy formats expose a bitrate control; lossless formats keep every sample. The result is validated, played back for comparison and offered as a download with its true byte size.
- Inputs: MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG, Opus, AIFF, AMR, WMA
- Outputs: audio
- How to use:
  1. Add an MP3, WAV, FLAC, M4A, OGG, Opus, AIFF, AMR or WMA file. Bench decodes it and shows duration, sample rate and channels.
  2. Pick the output format. Choose a bitrate for lossy formats or a lower sample rate to save space.
  3. Run the converter. The engine is downloaded the first time and cached afterwards.
  4. Preview the result and download it. If the requested format is unavailable, Bench says so instead of faking the output.
- Common uses: Turn a WAV recording into a small MP3.; Convert an M4A voice memo to WAV for editing.; Produce a FLAC master from a lossless source.
- Limits: MP3 output uses libmp3lame and AAC uses FFmpeg's encoder; both are lossy and re-encoding lossy audio again can add artefacts. Very long files are bounded by the 30-minute / 100 MB limits. The first conversion downloads the ~31 MB engine.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding run inside your browser. Files are read from local memory into temporary object URLs and are never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench. The FFmpeg.wasm engine is downloaded once from this site (same origin) and runs entirely on your device.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Which formats can I convert between?
    A: MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG Vorbis, Opus and AIFF in any direction the encoder supports, plus decoding of AMR, WMA, Speex and more.
  - Q: Why is the first conversion slow?
    A: The FFmpeg.wasm engine (~31 MB) is downloaded once and cached by your browser. Later conversions start instantly.
  - Q: Does converting lose quality?
    A: Converting to WAV, FLAC or AIFF is lossless. Converting to MP3, AAC, OGG or Opus is lossy; converting lossy to lossy can add artefacts, so start from the best source you have.

### Audio Compressor
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/audio/compress/
- Category: Convert
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Reduce an audio file's size by lowering bitrate, downmixing to mono and trimming the sample rate.
- What it does: Re-encodes audio at a lower bitrate, optionally mono, to cut file size while keeping the content. It reports the exact before and after size and the byte saving so you can judge the trade-off.
- Inputs: MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG, Opus, AIFF, AMR, WMA
- Outputs: audio
- How to use:
  1. Add a file. Bench reports its current size, duration and bitrate.
  2. Choose a lower bitrate. 128 kbps is fine for speech; 192-256 kbps suits music.
  3. Run the compressor and compare the before/after sizes.
  4. Preview, then download. If the file is already small, Bench tells you instead of inflating it.
- Common uses: Fit a podcast under a size limit.; Shrink voice notes before emailing.; Prepare spoken audio for a phone system.
- Limits: Lossy re-encoding is irreversible: the discarded detail cannot be recovered. Compressing an already-compressed file twice adds artefacts. Lossless inputs (WAV/FLAC) compress best.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding run inside your browser. Files are read from local memory into temporary object URLs and are never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench. The FFmpeg.wasm engine is downloaded once from this site (same origin) and runs entirely on your device.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Is my file uploaded?
    A: No. Processing happens in your browser and the file is never sent to Bench or a third party.

### Audio to WAV
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/audio/to-wav/
- Category: Convert
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Decode any supported audio file and export a universally compatible, uncompressed WAV file.
- What it does: Uses the browser's own decoder to turn your audio into uncompressed PCM WAV. WAV plays everywhere and is the safest format for editing, at the cost of a large file.
- Inputs: MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG, Opus, AIFF, AMR, WMA
- Outputs: audio
- How to use:
  1. Add any audio file your browser can decode.
  2. Choose channels and sample rate, or keep the originals.
  3. Bench writes a standard 16-bit PCM WAV and offers it for download.
- Common uses: Prepare audio for a video editor.; Convert a compressed file for a CD or hardware device.
- Limits: WAV is uncompressed, so files are large (roughly 10 MB per minute of stereo 44.1 kHz). Sample rates above the source offer no real gain.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding run inside your browser. Files are read from local memory into temporary object URLs and are never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench. The FFmpeg.wasm engine is downloaded once from this site (same origin) and runs entirely on your device.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Is my file uploaded?
    A: No. Processing happens in your browser and the file is never sent to Bench or a third party.

### Audio to MP3
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/audio/to-mp3/

- Status: Ready
- Summary: Encode any audio file to MP3 with libmp3lame at a bitrate you choose.

- Outputs: audio
- How to use:
  1. Add an audio file.
  2. Choose a bitrate: 128 kbps for speech, 192-320 kbps for music.
  3. Run the encoder and download the MP3.
- Common uses: Make a shareable MP3 from a WAV.; Produce a small file for a voice menu.
- Limits: MP3 is lossy and cannot store more channels than its container allows. Re-encoding an existing MP3 will not improve quality.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding run inside your browser. Files are read from local memory into temporary object URLs and are never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench. The FFmpeg.wasm engine is downloaded once from this site (same origin) and runs entirely on your device.

  - Q: Is my file uploaded?
    A: No. Processing happens in your browser and the file is never sent to Bench or a third party.

### Audio to FLAC
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/audio/to-flac/
- Category: Convert
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Encode audio to lossless, compressed FLAC - smaller than WAV with no quality loss.
- What it does: FLAC stores every sample of the original with lossless compression, so it is typically 40-60% smaller than WAV while remaining a perfect copy of the source audio.
- Inputs: MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG, Opus, AIFF, AMR, WMA
- Outputs: audio
- How to use:

  2. Keep channels and sample rate, or adjust them.
  3. Run the encoder and download the FLAC file.
- Common uses: Archive recordings losslessly.; Halve a WAV's size without losing quality.
- Limits: Encoding a lossy source to FLAC keeps the lossy artefacts - FLAC preserves what you give it, it cannot restore detail. FLAC is not supported by every legacy device.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding run inside your browser. Files are read from local memory into temporary object URLs and are never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench. The FFmpeg.wasm engine is downloaded once from this site (same origin) and runs entirely on your device.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Is my file uploaded?
    A: No. Processing happens in your browser and the file is never sent to Bench or a third party.

### Audio to Base64
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/audio/audio-to-base64/
- Category: Developer Utilities
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Encode an audio file as a Base64 string or a data URI for embedding in code.
- What it does: Reads the file and produces a Base64 string plus a ready-to-paste data URI. Base64 grows the payload by about 33%. Use it for small assets embedded in CSS, HTML or JSON, not for streaming media.
- Inputs: MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG, Opus, AIFF, AMR, WMA
- Outputs: text
- How to use:
  1. Add an audio file.
  2. Choose whether to include the data URI prefix.
  3. Copy the Base64 string or the data URI.
- Common uses: Embed a short sound in a HTML/CSS demo.; Paste a tiny clip into a JSON fixture.
- Limits: Large files become very large strings. Browsers may struggle to embed multi-megabyte data URIs.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding run inside your browser. Files are read from local memory into temporary object URLs and are never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench. The FFmpeg.wasm engine is downloaded once from this site (same origin) and runs entirely on your device.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Is my file uploaded?
    A: No. Processing happens in your browser and the file is never sent to Bench or a third party.

### Base64 to Audio
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/audio/base64-to-audio/
- Category: Developer Utilities
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Decode a Base64 string or data URI back into a playable, downloadable audio file.
- What it does: Paste a Base64 string or a full data URI and Bench reconstructs the original audio bytes for playback and download.
- Inputs: MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG, Opus, AIFF, AMR, WMA
- Outputs: audio
- How to use:
  1. Paste a Base64 string or data URI.
  2. Run the tool. Bench detects the audio type from the data URI or the file signature.
  3. Play or download the reconstructed file.
- Common uses: Recover an audio file pasted from an API response.; Test a data URI.
- Limits: A bare Base64 payload without a data URI may not carry a MIME type; Bench then guesses from the decoded bytes.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding run inside your browser. Files are read from local memory into temporary object URLs and are never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench. The FFmpeg.wasm engine is downloaded once from this site (same origin) and runs entirely on your device.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Is my file uploaded?
    A: No. Processing happens in your browser and the file is never sent to Bench or a third party.

### Audio Trimmer
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/audio/trimmer/
- Category: Edit & Design
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Cut a section out of an audio file with an interactive waveform and export the exact range.
- What it does: Decodes the file, draws its waveform and lets you drag precise start and end points. Export the selected range losslessly to WAV or re-encode to MP3.
- Inputs: MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG, Opus, AIFF, AMR, WMA
- Outputs: audio
- How to use:
  1. Add an audio file. The waveform and duration appear.
  2. Drag the handles or type the start and end times.
  3. Play the selection to check it.
  4. Export the trimmed audio.
- Common uses: Remove silence from the start of a recording.; Cut a clip out of a longer track.; Extract a radio segment.
- Limits: Trimming is sample-accurate to about one millisecond. MP3 has a small encoder delay/padding that can shift the very start by a few milliseconds.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding run inside your browser. Files are read from local memory into temporary object URLs and are never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench. The FFmpeg.wasm engine is downloaded once from this site (same origin) and runs entirely on your device.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Is my file uploaded?
    A: No. Processing happens in your browser and the file is never sent to Bench or a third party.

### Silence Remover
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/audio/silence-remover/
- Category: Clean & Enhance
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Detect silent gaps and remove them, or keep the gaps but trim the leading and trailing silence.
- What it does: Scans for silence below a threshold you set and either strips it out or reports it as a map. Useful for tightening voice recordings and podcasts.
- Inputs: MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG, Opus, AIFF, AMR, WMA
- Outputs: audio, text
- How to use:
  1. Add a recording.
  2. Pick a threshold, or lower it if quiet speech is being cut.
  3. Choose to strip silence or just map it.
  4. Export the result or copy the gap map.
- Common uses: Tighten a voice-over.; Cut dead air from interviews.; Find where the talking starts.
- Limits: Aggressive thresholds can clip quiet speech. Removing silence changes timing, so do not use it on music.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding run inside your browser. Files are read from local memory into temporary object URLs and are never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench. The FFmpeg.wasm engine is downloaded once from this site (same origin) and runs entirely on your device.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Is my file uploaded?
    A: No. Processing happens in your browser and the file is never sent to Bench or a third party.

### Audio Joiner
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/audio/joiner/
- Category: Edit & Design
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Merge two or more audio files into one track, in the order you choose, with optional crossfade.
- What it does: Combines files end to end, resampling and re-encoding to a single consistent output. Add a crossfade to blend tracks smoothly.
- Inputs: MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG, Opus, AIFF, AMR, WMA
- Outputs: audio

  2. Set a crossfade if you want tracks to blend.
  3. Choose the output format.
  4. Run the joiner and download the merged track.
- Common uses: Stitch audiobook chapters together.; Combine several voice memos.; Build a continuous DJ-style mix.
- Limits: Files with different sample rates or channel counts are resampled to match the first file. Joining very many or very long files increases memory use.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding run inside your browser. Files are read from local memory into temporary object URLs and are never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench. The FFmpeg.wasm engine is downloaded once from this site (same origin) and runs entirely on your device.

### Change Speed
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/audio/speed/
- Category: Edit & Design
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Speed up or slow down audio while keeping the pitch the same (time-stretch).
- What it does: Stretches or compresses time using FFmpeg's atempo filter so speech stays intelligible at 0.5x-3x speed without the chipmunk effect.
- Inputs: MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG, Opus, AIFF, AMR, WMA
- Outputs: audio
- How to use:
  1. Add a file.
  2. Move the speed slider.
  3. Export the sped-up or slowed-down audio.
- Common uses: Speed up a slow lecture.; Slow down a fast passage to transcribe it.
- Limits: This is pitch-preserving time-stretch: at extremes the result can sound slightly metallic. For a tape-style pitch change, use the Pitch Shifter instead.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding run inside your browser. Files are read from local memory into temporary object URLs and are never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench. The FFmpeg.wasm engine is downloaded once from this site (same origin) and runs entirely on your device.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Is my file uploaded?
    A: No. Processing happens in your browser and the file is never sent to Bench or a third party.

### Pitch Shifter
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/audio/pitch/
- Category: Edit & Design
- Status: Experimental
- Summary: Shift the pitch up or down. Speakers' pitch can be raised or lowered for anonymity or effects.
- What it does: Shifts pitch by resampling and compensating with time-stretch so the duration stays similar. The result is an estimate and can introduce artefacts at large shifts.
- Inputs: MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG, Opus, AIFF, AMR, WMA
- Outputs: audio
- How to use:
  1. Add a file.
  2. Choose how many semitones to shift.
  3. Export the shifted audio.
- Common uses: Raise a voice for anonymity.; Tune a recording slightly.; Create a character voice.
- Limits: This build has no formant-preserving pitch shifter, so large shifts also change the perceived voice character and can sound artefacted. Small shifts (±2 semitones) are cleanest.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding run inside your browser. Files are read from local memory into temporary object URLs and are never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench. The FFmpeg.wasm engine is downloaded once from this site (same origin) and runs entirely on your device.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Is my file uploaded?
    A: No. Processing happens in your browser and the file is never sent to Bench or a third party.

### Volume & Normalise
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/audio/volume-adjust/
- Category: Clean & Enhance
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Change the loudness by a fixed amount or normalise to a target peak, with clipping protection.
- What it does: Either applies a gain offset you set or normalises the whole file to a target peak level. A safety limiter prevents clipping when you boost.
- Inputs: MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG, Opus, AIFF, AMR, WMA
- Outputs: audio
- How to use:
  1. Add a file.
  2. Choose fixed gain or normalise-to-peak.
  3. Set the amount.
  4. Export the adjusted audio.
- Common uses: Make a quiet recording audible.; Match two clips to a similar level.; Reduce a too-loud track.
- Limits: Normalising to peak does not make quiet passages loud; it only scales so the loudest point hits the target. Boosting heavily raises the noise floor.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding run inside your browser. Files are read from local memory into temporary object URLs and are never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench. The FFmpeg.wasm engine is downloaded once from this site (same origin) and runs entirely on your device.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Is my file uploaded?
    A: No. Processing happens in your browser and the file is never sent to Bench or a third party.

### Noise Reducer
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/audio/noise-reducer/
- Category: Clean & Enhance
- Status: Experimental
- Summary: Reduce steady background noise (hiss, hum, air conditioning) with a real FFT denoiser.
- What it does: Runs a genuine spectral-subtraction denoiser (FFmpeg's afftdn) with an adjustable noise floor. It reduces constant broadband noise rather than transient sounds.
- Inputs: MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG, Opus, AIFF, AMR, WMA
- Outputs: audio
- How to use:
  1. Add a recording with steady background noise.
  2. Set the noise floor to just above the hiss.
  3. Choose how much to reduce.
  4. Export and compare.
- Common uses: Clean a noisy interview recording.; Reduce air-conditioner hum in a podcast.; Improve a phone recording.
- Limits: This is spectral subtraction, not an AI model: heavy reduction can introduce a watery 'musical noise' artefact. It targets constant noise, not speech or music.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding run inside your browser. Files are read from local memory into temporary object URLs and are never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench. The FFmpeg.wasm engine is downloaded once from this site (same origin) and runs entirely on your device.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Is my file uploaded?
    A: No. Processing happens in your browser and the file is never sent to Bench or a third party.

### Voice Enhancer
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/audio/voice-enhancer/
- Category: Clean & Enhance
- Status: Experimental
- Summary: Brighten and control speech with a high-pass, EQ and gentle compression chain.
- What it does: Applies a speech-tuned chain: high-pass to remove rumble, a presence boost, gentle dynamic compression and a limiter. It improves intelligibility on dry speech.
- Inputs: MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG, Opus, AIFF, AMR, WMA
- Outputs: audio
- How to use:
  1. Add a speech recording.
  2. Adjust the presence and rumble cut.
  3. Choose a compression amount.
  4. Export and compare.
- Common uses: Make a podcast host sound clearer.; Improve a webcam microphone recording.
- Limits: This is deterministic signal processing, not AI restoration. It cannot remove reverb or add missing detail, and heavy compression reduces dynamics.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding run inside your browser. Files are read from local memory into temporary object URLs and are never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench. The FFmpeg.wasm engine is downloaded once from this site (same origin) and runs entirely on your device.

### Loudness Normaliser (LUFS)
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/audio/loudness-normalizer/
- Category: Clean & Enhance
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Normalise to a broadcast loudness target in LUFS with true-peak limiting.
- What it does: Measures integrated loudness with the ITU-R BS.1770/EBU R128 loudnorm filter and normalises to your target, with a true-peak ceiling so it never clips.
- Inputs: MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG, Opus, AIFF, AMR, WMA
- Outputs: audio, text
- How to use:
  1. Add a file.
  2. Choose a loudness target for your platform.
  3. Export the normalised audio and read the measured before/after values.
- Common uses: Bring a podcast to -16 LUFS.; Match a video upload to -14 LUFS.; Prepare audio for broadcast at -23 LUFS.
- Limits: Two-pass normalisation is used, so the file is analysed first. Extremely dynamic material may be limited more than expected.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding run inside your browser. Files are read from local memory into temporary object URLs and are never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench. The FFmpeg.wasm engine is downloaded once from this site (same origin) and runs entirely on your device.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Is my file uploaded?
    A: No. Processing happens in your browser and the file is never sent to Bench or a third party.

### Voice Recorder
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/audio/recorder/
- Category: Record & Microphone
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Record from your microphone in the browser, preview it and download a WAV or WebM/Opus file.
- What it does: Requests microphone access only when you click record, shows a live level meter and a timer, and lets you trim and export the take. Nothing is uploaded.
- Inputs: MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG, Opus, AIFF, AMR, WMA
- Outputs: audio
- How to use:
  1. Click Start and allow microphone access when your browser asks.
  2. Watch the level meter and record your take.
  3. Stop, preview the recording and trim if needed.
  4. Download the file. It is created locally; nothing is uploaded.
- Common uses: Record a voice memo.; Capture a quick podcast segment.; Practise a presentation.
- Limits: Microphone access must be allowed by the browser and the site's permissions policy. WAV export is lossless and large; WebM/Opus is smaller. Recording stops if you close the tab or revoke the microphone.
- Privacy: Recording uses the browser MediaRecorder API. Your audio is captured from the microphone into local memory, is never uploaded and is discarded when you leave the page or clear it. Bench does not retain recordings.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Is my file uploaded?
    A: No. Processing happens in your browser and the file is never sent to Bench or a third party.

### BPM & Key Detector
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/audio/bpm-detector/
- Category: Music & Sound
- Status: Experimental
- Summary: Estimate the tempo (BPM) of a track and suggest a likely musical key from its spectrum.
- What it does: Estimates tempo from onset energy and suggests a key from chroma-like spectral energy. Both are estimates and can be wrong on complex or non-percussive material.
- Inputs: MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG, Opus, AIFF, AMR, WMA
- Outputs: text
- How to use:
  1. Add a track with a clear beat.
  2. Run the analysis.
  3. Read the estimated BPM and key.
- Common uses: Find the BPM for a mashup.; Get a starting key for a cover.
- Limits: Tempo detection needs a steady beat; it struggles with free-tempo and heavily syncopated music. Key detection is a coarse spectral estimate and should be treated as a hint only.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding run inside your browser. Files are read from local memory into temporary object URLs and are never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench. The FFmpeg.wasm engine is downloaded once from this site (same origin) and runs entirely on your device.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Is my file uploaded?
    A: No. Processing happens in your browser and the file is never sent to Bench or a third party.

### ID3 Tag Editor
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/audio/id3-editor/
- Category: Metadata & Privacy
- Status: Experimental
- Summary: View and rewrite common ID3/tag fields (title, artist, album, genre) and export a new copy.
- What it does: Copies the audio stream and writes updated metadata using FFmpeg, so the audio content is preserved. The output is a new file; the original is never modified.
- Inputs: MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG, Opus, AIFF, AMR, WMA

  2. Fill in the tags you want (empty fields are left as-is or cleared, as shown).
  3. Export the re-tagged copy and verify it in the metadata viewer.
- Common uses: Fix a mislabelled track.; Add artist and album to a rip.
- Limits: Stream copy preserves the audio bytes but may re-wrap the container. Some players cache tags aggressively. Not all tag frames are editable in this build.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding run inside your browser. Files are read from local memory into temporary object URLs and are never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench. The FFmpeg.wasm engine is downloaded once from this site (same origin) and runs entirely on your device.

### Duplicate Audio Finder
- URL: https://bench.progeni.live/audio/duplicate-finder/
- Category: Metadata & Privacy
- Status: Ready
- Summary: Compare several audio files and find exact duplicates using a content hash.
- What it does: Computes a hash of the decoded audio (not just the bytes) so the same audio saved in two containers is detected. Similar-sounding but different files are reported as distinct.
- Inputs: MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/M4A, OGG, Opus, AIFF, AMR, WMA
- Outputs: text
- How to use:
  1. Add two or more files.
  2. Run the comparison.
  3. Read which files are exact duplicates.
- Common uses: Clean a music library.; Check for repeated voice memos.
- Limits: Matching is exact on decoded samples at the original sample rate. Different bitrates of the same song are NOT flagged as duplicates - that would be approximate similarity, which this build does not claim to do.
- Privacy: Decoding, editing and encoding run inside your browser. Files are read from local memory into temporary object URLs and are never uploaded, logged or stored by Bench. The FFmpeg.wasm engine is downloaded once from this site (same origin) and runs entirely on your device.
- FAQ:
  - Q: Is my file uploaded?
    A: No. Processing happens in your browser and the file is never sent to Bench or a third party.

## Tools that are not shipped

These entries are documented so that assistants do not invent a working feature or link.

### Image toolkit
- Image to Text OCR (deferred): An OCR engine and language pack are not bundled. Shipping Tesseract.js with an English model adds roughly 10-15 MB to the static deployment and needs a dedicated loading, cancellation and accuracy test pass. Deferred rather than faked.
- Searchable PDF (deferred): Depends on the OCR engine and a PDF text-layer writer. Neither is available in the current dependency set.
- PDF to Image (deferred): PDF decoding requires PDF.js or a server engine. Adding a full PDF renderer for one tool was not justified in this build.
- HEIC / HEIF Converter (deferred): No HEIC decoder is bundled. Browser support is inconsistent and libheif adds a large WASM payload; files are rejected with an explanation instead of producing a broken output.
- Video to GIF (deferred): Requires video seeking, frame extraction and a bounded duration workflow. Image-only GIF tools are implemented; video decoding is deferred.
- Barcode Reader (deferred): The bundled QR decoder does not read 1D barcodes. A separate decoder was not added without a tested implementation.
- HTML to Image (deferred): Requires an HTML/CSS rasteriser with strict sanitisation. Deferred to avoid an unsafe rendering surface.
- Raster to SVG Vector Trace (deferred): Not implemented. Bench does not embed a raster image inside SVG and call it vector tracing.
- CMYK / ICC Conversion (deferred): Canvas is sRGB and does not expose colour-managed CMYK transforms. A correct implementation needs a colour-management engine and profile handling.
- Image URL Inspector (deferred): Remote fetching would create SSRF and CORS risks, and the project has no isolated fetch service. The tool is intentionally unavailable.
- AI Background Remover (unavailable): No inference provider is configured. Bench does not simulate AI results, and the project has no funded GPU endpoint. The provider adapter interface is present so a vetted local or hosted model can be added without changing the tool registry.
- AI Background Replacement (unavailable): No inference provider is configured. Bench does not simulate AI results, and the project has no funded GPU endpoint. The provider adapter interface is present so a vetted local or hosted model can be added without changing the tool registry.
- AI Object Removal / Inpainting (unavailable): No inference provider is configured. Bench does not simulate AI results, and the project has no funded GPU endpoint. The provider adapter interface is present so a vetted local or hosted model can be added without changing the tool registry.
- AI Image Upscaler (unavailable): No inference provider is configured. Bench does not simulate AI results, and the project has no funded GPU endpoint. The provider adapter interface is present so a vetted local or hosted model can be added without changing the tool registry.
- AI Denoise & Restore (unavailable): No inference provider is configured. Bench does not simulate AI results, and the project has no funded GPU endpoint. The provider adapter interface is present so a vetted local or hosted model can be added without changing the tool registry.
- AI Photo Colorization (unavailable): No inference provider is configured. Bench does not simulate AI results, and the project has no funded GPU endpoint. The provider adapter interface is present so a vetted local or hosted model can be added without changing the tool registry.
- AI Low-Light Enhancement (unavailable): No inference provider is configured. Bench does not simulate AI results, and the project has no funded GPU endpoint. The provider adapter interface is present so a vetted local or hosted model can be added without changing the tool registry.
- AI Portrait Background Blur (unavailable): No inference provider is configured. Bench does not simulate AI results, and the project has no funded GPU endpoint. The provider adapter interface is present so a vetted local or hosted model can be added without changing the tool registry.
- AI Product Photo Enhancement (unavailable): No inference provider is configured. Bench does not simulate AI results, and the project has no funded GPU endpoint. The provider adapter interface is present so a vetted local or hosted model can be added without changing the tool registry.
- AI Face Enhancement (unavailable): No inference provider is configured. Bench does not simulate AI results, and the project has no funded GPU endpoint. The provider adapter interface is present so a vetted local or hosted model can be added without changing the tool registry.
- AI Caption & Alt Text (unavailable): No inference provider is configured. Bench does not simulate AI results, and the project has no funded GPU endpoint. The provider adapter interface is present so a vetted local or hosted model can be added without changing the tool registry.

### Audio toolkit
- Audio Transcription (deferred): Requires a speech-recognition model (e.g. Whisper). Running it in-browser needs a large model download and the site's CSP blocks external APIs (connect-src 'self'). Ship a verified adapter before publishing a page.
- Text to Speech (unavailable): The browser SpeechSynthesis API can speak text but cannot reliably capture the output to a file, so a real downloadable MP3/WAV is not possible without a TTS engine or provider. Not offered rather than faked.
- Vocal Remover / Stem Separation (deferred): Requires a real source-separation model (e.g. Demucs/Spleeter). A centre-channel cancellation is not genuine separation, so this is deferred until a licensed model can be shipped.
- AI Noise Reduction (deferred): Requires a licensed neural model. The shipped afftdn denoiser is real spectral processing, not AI, and is offered honestly as the Noise Reducer instead.
- Audio Restoration (deferred): Needs a restoration model. Deterministic filters (declick, declip) exist in the engine and could ship as an experimental tool; full restoration is deferred.
- Speaker Diarization (unavailable): Depends on a speaker-recognition model and, typically, a transcript. No local model is shipped, so labels cannot be produced from real results.
- Speech Translation (deferred): Depends on transcription plus a translation service. External APIs are blocked by the site's CSP, so this is deferred with transcription.
- System / Tab Audio Capture (deferred): getDisplayMedia with audio capture is not supported consistently across browsers and platforms. Deferred rather than shipped with silent failures.
